description: Kemet Nova is a multidisciplinary Egyptian team for NASA Space Apps 2025, tackling “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” We’re building a decision-support tool that helps farmers adapt to climate shifts, plan resilient crop rotations, and protect soil health using NASA Earth observation data. Our team combines engineering, full-stack development, AI/ML, chemistry, pharmacy, and design to turn satellite data into practical solutions for food security and sustainable agriculture.
summary: FieldShift is an intelligent, web-based Decision Support Tool designed to help smallholder farmers and agricultural advisors in the Egyptian land optimize crop rotations and irrigation schedules. By integrating NASA POWER historical climate data with the FAO-56 scientific water-balance methodology and local field inputs (soil type, drainage, and irrigation practices), FieldShift calculates precise crop water requirements (ET_c) and screens for seasonal heat stress. It addresses the urgent challenge of water scarcity and climate unpredictability by replacing guesswork with transparent, explainable AI recommendations—empowering farmers to conserve up to 20% of water, improve soil health, and reduce financial risk without forcing blind changes to their livelihoods.
details:
FieldShift is a smart Decision Support Tool that transforms traditional crop rotation in the Egyptian Land into data-driven, climate-resilient decisions. Its primary goals are to optimize water consumption, mitigate seasonal heat stress ,enhance soil fertility, and provide transparent, explainable insights tailored to local farming realities (using local units like Feddans and Qirats).

How It Works:

1-Satellite Climate Ingestion: Retrieves 11 years of daily historical meteorological data (temperature, solar radiation, wind speed, humidity) via the NASA POWER Daily AG API for the farmer's coordinates.

2-Scientific Water & Heat Modeling: Applies the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith equation to compute Reference Evapotranspiration (ET_0) and scales it using four-stage crop coefficients (K_c) to determine exact crop water demand.

3-Local Field Calibration: Adjusts satellite insights using a farmer-friendly diagnostic survey (soil texture, drainage speed, canal rotation intervals, and irrigation methods like flood, raised beds, or laser leveling).

4-Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) & Explainable AI: Filters unsuitable crops and ranks rotation alternatives across key priorities (water efficiency, heat tolerance, soil health, and relative income). Instead of black-box commands, it provides clear explanations, benefits, and risk warnings (e.g., advising small-scale trials for new crops).

Tools, Data & Technologies Used:

NASA Datasets: NASA POWER Daily AG API (Climate & Energy parameters).

Scientific Standards: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith Evapotranspiration model & Egyptian Agricultural Research Center validation benchmarks.

Software & Development Stack: Modern Web Technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript / React) for an accessible, mobile-friendly Arabic/English interface, alongside Python/JavaScript calculation engines for agro-climatic modeling and MCDA scoring.
projectRefs: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56: Crop Evapotranspiration
